findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional. Case: normal use - running either documented clients/jobs command. The filters marker encloses the entire `const projectFilters = { ... };` declaration in the starter contracts (lines 15–24), but `_filters` returns only its property lines. Replacing that section therefore emits invalid top-level TypeScript and leaves the renamed filters variable undefined. Every generated contracts package fails to compile. Preserve the declaration around the generated properties.
findings.title: Preserve the filters object declaration in generated contracts

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional. Case: normal use - generating the documented clients or jobs API. This replacement recognizes `project:` but excludes `project[`, so the starter's `encodeCursor` parameter becomes `featureItem` while `project[sortBy]` becomes `client[sortBy]` or `job[sortBy]`. The source expression is in projects.service.ts:63. Those identifiers are undeclared, causing every generated server package to fail compilation; bypassing type checks also breaks cursor creation. Rename indexed references consistently with the parameter.
findings.title: Rename indexed cursor references along with their parameter

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional. Case: normal use - generating a feature with two links, such as `client:link(clients)` and `project:link(projects)`. Each iteration emits `const linkedInput`, `crossOrganisation`, `crossRefused`, `deletedLink` and `deletedRefused`, and line 121 concatenates them into one function scope. The resulting API test has duplicate lexical declarations and cannot load in Vitest. Give each field's checks a separate block or distinct variable names.
findings.title: Scope the generated validation case for each link field

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional. Case: normal use - clients have a name, jobs require a client link, and tasks link to jobs. The generated tasks tests call `linkedItem` to create a job. This helper copies the required `clientId` property's documentation example into the request without creating its client. Link examples come from the fixed kind-table sample, so the jobs API rejects that nonexistent client with 400 while this helper expects 201. Generate valid required dependencies through their APIs so linked features' tests run successfully.
findings.title: Create required linked dependencies instead of using example UUIDs

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional. Case: normal use - generating `status:status(active|planned)`. `_field_cases` selects the kind-table sample `planned`, but this line also assigns `options[1]` (`planned`) to the supposedly nonmatching record. Both records match the filter, so the generated assertions expecting one ID and one CSV data row fail despite a correctly functioning API. Select an option unequal to the matching record's actual value.
findings.title: Choose a status filter fixture different from the matching value
